Let \(x=\left(\frac12\right)^{n-1}\). Then \(S_n=3-x\) and \(S_{2n}=3-\frac12x^2\).

The inequality becomes
\[
\frac{34}{33}<\frac{3-\frac12x^2}{3-x}<\frac{16}{15}.
\]

Left inequality:
\[
33x^2-68x+6<0
\]
whose relevant root is approximately \(0.092\), so \(x>0.092\).

Right inequality:
\[
15x^2-32x+6>0
\]
whose smaller root is approximately \(0.208\), so for \(x\le 1\), \(x<0.208\).

Thus
\[
0.092<x<0.208.
\]
Since \(x=(1/2)^{n-1}\), the only power of \(1/2\) in this interval is
\[
x=\frac18=\left(\frac12\right)^3.
\]
So \(n-1=3\), giving \(n=4\).

The sum of all such \(n\) is \(\boxed{4}\).
